gate_a_failure_modes.bug_reframed_as_insight: SUSPECTED: 'reuse saving grows under SLO because reused hosts are the cheapest idle reserve' - reuse share of node-quarters stayed ~0.30; supported mechanism is weaker (part of added reserve sits on low-embodied hosts). Flagged for refinement.

weaknesses: Unsupported causal claim in the Abstract, Introduction (3) and Conclusion: 'the reuse saving rose to 0.812% because reused hosts are the cheapest idle reserve' / 'because idle reserve is where low-embodied reused hosts are cheapest'. The log shows only that the reuse plan's SLO price was slightly lower (0.785 vs 0.823%). It gives no reserve composition by SKU. old_gpu, not green_gpu, has the lowest embodied carbon (0 vs 2,860 kgCO2e). green_gpu also has 50 W lower idle power, which is an alternative explanation. The paper's own headroom sweep cuts against the claim: the reuse-host share fell from 0.303 to 0.280 as LC headroom rose from 1 to 10, while Y moved only 0.775 to 0.777%. The effect is 0.037 pp, with no Monte Carlo confidence intervals and a reserve-loop tolerance (0.05% of demand, 1.05 overshoot) that could produce differences of similar size. Either report reserve composition and CIs, or restate this as an observed small difference without a mechanism.

Misreported and overstated SLO validation (Section 5.4): 'Every plan met its target in independent validation (worst region-quarter 0.96-1.07% for a 1% target and 0.10-0.13% for 0.1%)'. The log gives 0.96-1.06% and 0.10-0.12%, and only for reuse plans; no-reuse validation is not logged. Several validated values exceed their targets (1.06% > 1%, 0.12% > 0.1%), so 'met' needs a statement about sampling error (about ±0.014 pp at 50,000 samples for 0.1%).

Figure/text mismatches. The Figure 2 caption claims the CXL multiplier 'alone determines the sign of the saving', but the plotted bars flip sign for the peak-power delta (-2.30), SSD embodied carbon (-2.49), grid CI (-0.41), idle-power delta (-0.41) and others. Figure 6 plots m=3, epsilon=0.01 points at k=2 and k=0.5 that are neither in Table 3 nor in the log. Table 3 silently drops two logged rows. Y_expected for m=3 is given as 0.480%, while the multiplier sweep in Figure 4 gives 0.475% at m=3, and this is not reconciled. Figure 3's header says 'naive 0.19%' and 'Z=+0.00pp' against 0.195% and 0.005 pp in the text. Figures 3, 5 and 6 contain internal labels ('C2/C3 measurements', 'A100-class vs H100-class', raw config keys) that are undefined in the paper.

Over-claiming given the placeholder GPU parameters. The Abstract headlines mixed- and dirty-grid fleet savings (0.68%, 0.10%) and an SLO result without saying that their sign and size depend on the placeholder CXL multiplier, whose range alone swings the node-level saving from -10.72% to +5.88%. The fuzzy alpha=0 interval already reaches Y=0.000. 'Public and swept parameters' overstates provenance, since only the GPU AFR is public (Section 4.1 itself says 'All other parameters are engineering assumptions'). The design implication that reuse hosts 'belong ... in reserve' rests on the unsupported mechanism above. Statements that the reliability-aware plan 'never chose a plan worse than no reuse' and that the fuzzy 'lower bound never fell below zero' are guaranteed by construction, because no reuse is feasible, and should not be presented as evidence of robustness.

Key implementation details are missing from Section 4: the leased-capacity carbon premium (1.3x), the shipping carbon (300 kgCO2e per node), the default utilization cap (0.8) and LC headroom multiplier (3), green_gpu and old_gpu power, platform embodied carbon, design life and maximum age, initial-fleet ages, previous-generation GPU Weibull shape, all cost parameters for the Pareto front, and how the correlation dispersion k was chosen. There is also a notation clash (H for both cumulative hazard and hours per quarter), an age-unit inconsistency in the AFR calibration, and unexpanded acronyms (CXL, PUE, SECDED, NUMA).

The Abstract and Introduction still overstate the SLO mechanism: 'the reuse saving rose slightly, to 0.812%, because about a fifth of the reuse plan's reserve sat on hosts with lower embodied carbon and idle power'. Table 3 shows that half of the 214 tCO2e gap is operational (115 t). A 50 W idle-power delta on 21.7% of the reserve explains only about 15 t of that. The rest is more plausibly explained by the reuse plan adding 3.6% less reserve capacity (1,272.6 vs 1,320.3 node-equivalents; 30.6 sit on previous-generation hosts with higher idle power per unit capacity), which the paper does not explain. Section 5.4's 'reflecting the lower embodied carbon and slightly lower idle power of reuse-based hosts' repeats the overreach. The effect (0.037 pp) comes from a single decomposition at one setting with no seed variation. Attribute only the embodied half, explain the capacity difference, or soften the Abstract to 'the reuse plan's reserve emitted 5% less'.

The entry age of reused parts, a_0, is never given a value, although it defines the central premise that reused parts are old. The log gives 5 years for green_gpu DIMMs and SSDs and 4 years for old_gpu parts. Initial-fleet ages (6/8/4 quarters for current-generation hosts), logistics carbon per repair (5/2/1 kgCO2e) and the scope of the 0.9 screening yield (locally harvested parts only) are also missing from Section 4 and Table 5.

Remaining figure, table and text mismatches. The Figure 3 caption describes 'Y plus cascading' in the right panel, but that panel plots only X, failure-blind and Y. Table 3 drops the spares-plus-logistics column (89 and 97 tCO2e in the log), so its columns do not sum to 'Added carbon'. Section 5.4 says Y rose 'from 0.480% to 0.500%' at m=3, while Table 4 lists 0.499. Figure 2 shows sensitivity bars for parameters (platform embodied carbon, SSD Weibull shape, new-host peak power, PUE) whose ranges and values are not given anywhere in the paper.

Some statements still go beyond the evidence. The Abstract's 'on mixed and dirty grids even the sign depends on the placeholder CXL slowdown' is attached to fleet savings that cannot be negative by construction, and node-level sign sensitivity was shown only for the mixed grid. The new design implication 'powering reserve hosts down when not needed matters more than which SKU holds it' is not evaluated: the model has no power-down state, and powered-down hosts may not count as instantaneous LC capacity under the SLO. 'At the target within sampling error' is generous for 0.13% against a 0.1% target, which is about 2 standard errors above it.

Presentation and structure. The accounting-convention table and the cost-carbon front, both used as Results evidence, now sit in an appendix after the references, which the venue guidelines do not provide for. About a third of page 11 is blank because of float placement. The beta_LC=1 baseline of the chance-constrained study is disclosed only parenthetically and should appear in Section 3.3 next to Eq. 5. No confidence intervals are reported for any Monte Carlo-derived quantity.

The SLO result is only partly explained, and seed coverage is narrow. The Abstract's 'because the reuse plan needed about 3% less reserve capacity' names a proximate cause whose own cause 'we did not isolate'. 'Stems mainly from the smaller reserve' is an inference rather than a measured attribution, although a 2.6-3.6% capacity reduction times about 3,300 tCO2e is the right order of magnitude. Seed replication (three seeds) covers only epsilon=0.001, k=0.5, m=1. The other eleven settings in Table 4 and Figure 6, and the '2.6x reserve' claim, are single-run, and Section 5.4 quotes the seed-0 value 0.812 without saying so.

The headline SLO price depends on unfitted correlation levels. 'Up to 0.82% extra carbon' in the Abstract and Introduction comes from k=0.5, which Table 6 describes as 'illustrative, not fitted'. The price roughly doubles from independent failures (0.30-0.31%) to k=0.5 (0.79-0.82%). The Abstract should state that k is illustrative, or report the independent-failure price alongside it.

The entry age a_0 is never swept. It now appears as 5 years for reused DIMMs and SSDs, and it is the parameter behind the premise that reused parts are old. The hazard multiplier m scales hazard magnitude, but it does not capture shifts along the Weibull wear-out curve (DIMM shape 1.6) that a different a_0 would produce. A sweep of a_0 = 3/5/7 years at fleet level would close this gap.

Unsupported detail and structure. 'External supply arrives pre-screened' (Section 3.1) is not in the evidence base; the log states only that the 0.9 yield applies to locally harvested parts. Section 5.5 still compresses four studies into one paragraph, and the evidence for three of them (Tables 5 and 7, Figure 7) sits in an appendix after the references. Page 11 has visible float whitespace. The main text uses exactly 12 of 12 pages.

The SLO mechanism is stated more generally than the evidence supports. The Abstract and Introduction explain the higher reuse saving under the SLO 'because the reuse plan needed about 3% less reserve capacity', and Section 5.4 says the reuse plan paid less 'in every setting'. The log's per-setting reserve table shows that at m=3 the reuse plan holds a larger reserve than the no-reuse plan in 5 of 6 settings (380.2 vs 372.9, 527.7 vs 516.3, 498.1 vs 491.2, 723.7 vs 722.7 and 798.0 vs 795.6 node-equivalent-quarters), yet it still pays a lower price. The smaller-reserve explanation therefore holds only at m=1 (and m=3, k=0.5, epsilon=0.001). The m=3 price advantage must come from reserve composition. The paper does not report this table, and its root cause remains unisolated. Scope the 'because' to m=1 and report the reserve table.

Two different reserve quantities share near-identical numbers without definition. Section 5.4 gives '1,274 ... node-equivalent-quarters' of reserve for the reuse plan, while Table 3 gives 1,272.6 of 'added reserve capacity' for the same setting (seed 0). The difference between the reserve target R_rt and the added installed capacity in the chance-constrained minus expected-value plan should be defined.

Evidence for several cited results is outside the main body or only in prose. The entry-age sweep and the reserve sizes appear only as inline numbers. The sensitivity ranges, accounting conventions and cost front sit in an appendix after the references, which the venue guidelines do not provide for. Figures 4 and 5 at 0.52 linewidth have small tick labels.

The scope of the significance claims should be stated more plainly. The blended three-grid fleet saving is under 1% (Y=0.775%), and the larger clean-grid figures and the cascading verdict rest on assumed or placeholder parameters with no executed GPU measurements. The Conclusion should say explicitly that the paper's contribution is the planning methodology and its break-even analyses, not the size of the savings.

post_cap_fidelity_fixes: Scoped the SLO mechanism: smaller reserve only in the decomposed m=1 setting; at m=3 the reserve target was not smaller in 5/6 settings, so composition drives the lower price
Distinguished reserve target sum R_rt from added installed capacity (Table 3)
Conclusion states contribution is method + break-evens, not savings size
Layout trims to keep main text within 12 pages
